help.title: How Roles & Permissions work
help.overview.title: The big picture
help.overview.body: Every login account in your company has a baseline role. You grant extra access by assigning custom roles to accounts within a specific scope (company, department, or zone). Permissions flow from the union of everything an account holds.
help.builtins.title: Built-in roles (read-only)
help.builtins.hint: You cannot edit or delete built-in roles. Use the Copy button to seed a new custom role from either one.
help.custom.title: Custom roles
help.custom.step1: Click "Add Role" (or Copy a built-in) to open the editor.
help.custom.step2: Give it a clear name — e.g. "Site Manager", "HR Viewer".
help.custom.step3: Tick the permissions it should grant, grouped by plugin and domain.
help.custom.step4: Save. The role is now available to assign.
help.assignment.title: Assigning a role
help.assignment.body: Open a role, click "Assign", then pick an account and a scope. The account receives that role's permissions — but only within the scope you choose.
help.assignment.effective: You can also set "Effective From" / "Effective To" to time-box the access — useful for contractors or temporary managers.
help.scope.department: Limited to people/resources of one department.
help.scope.zone: Limited to devices and access inside one zone.
help.accounts.title: Who can be assigned?
help.accounts.body: Only users with a login account appear in the assignment list. Employees tracked in Identity without a login (e.g. contractors with just a card) cannot hold a role — create a login account first in User Management.
help.example.title: Example
help.example.s1: • You create a custom role "HR Manager" with identity.user.* permissions.
help.example.s2: • You assign it to alice@company.com with scope = Department "HR".
help.example.s3: • Alice can now view/edit users in HR only. Anywhere else she stays a Member.
